coaching.headline: Three of five lanes went clean and we even opened with first blood, but our six won fights turned into zero towers or objectives while they cashed five of seven. That conversion gap turned a favorable start into a loss.
coaching.team: We opened with first blood, Terra onto Crunch at 1.7 minutes, and two lanes ran clean the whole game: Steel shut out Sevarog and Kira never lost to Drongo. Aurora held an early jungle edge over Khaimera before that lane evened out. The exception was mid, where Neon lost to Gideon from start to finish. Gideon finished with the match's biggest damage total, 67,562, and only one of our heroes itemized magic resist against him. That mid deficit showed up on the map: river buffs went 2-26 their way and towers finished 2-10. The fights told the same story. We won six fights outright and turned none of them into a tower or objective, while they cashed five of their seven wins. The two most expensive losses, at 10.4 near their Fangtooth and at 16.3 at their Inner Tower, both had an alive teammate who wasn't losing their lane sitting out while the rest fought and lost by three or more bodies. The fights at 18.8 and 26.8 were then started with our midlaner still pinned in his losing lane — the wrong calls with a fifth already stuck across the map. The game ended at 29.6 minutes with the full roster in a straight fight at their Core, lost 0-5. Next game: when a teammate is alive and holding their lane, get them into the fight before it starts. Both of the costliest losses had exactly that gap open.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The six-for-zero conversion gap, paired with winning-or-even teammates sitting out fights the rest then lost by three or more bodies. Steel was alive for the loss at 10.4 and Terra for the loss at 16.3. That combination, not the draft or the lanes, turned a favorable start into a loss.
coaching.whatWorked: The one clean pattern that worked: winning at our own Fangtooth. The teamfight at 21.7, won 3-1, was followed by our Fangtooth take at 22 minutes — the cleanest fight-to-objective conversion of the game.

perPlayer.5abbc223-5188-4aba-b698-820a7c5a2c00: Terra was caught out alone twice early, by Crunch at 5.2 minutes and by Khaimera at 8.4, before the lane with Crunch ever settled into its even read. Terra was also alive in that even lane at 16.3 and sat out the teamfight at their Inner Tower, lost 3-6. An even lane had nothing to lose by rotating into that one. The build also skipped Tainted Guard from its winning core (Fire Blossom, Tainted Guard, Inquisition) for Elafrost and Transference instead.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Kira's lane win over Drongo held clean all game and led the team in damage to heroes. The build went Vanquisher, Onixian Quiver and Scattershot, skipping the winning core of Solaris, Ashbringer and Imperator entirely. Every one of Kira's four deaths came right before a tower, an inhibitor, or the Core fell. The first two came at 10.5 and 16.7 minutes. The last two came at 25.7 and 29.6.
perPlayer.d9b59cab-b3f3-4044-83d5-2799f376355c: Neon's mid lane was lost to Gideon the entire game. Gideon walked away with the match's biggest damage total while our team carried only one hero itemized for magic resist. Neon died ten times, including a solo catch by Gideon at 15.4 minutes. Neon was also still pinned in that losing lane when the fights at 18.8 and 26.8 were started without him. With a fifth stuck across the map, those were the wrong fights to start, and the lane itself never got contested back.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Steel shut out Sevarog all game and led the team with 12 wards, but sat out the fight at 10.4 near their Fangtooth, lost 1 kill to 4 — a fight that came right after that Fangtooth had already fallen at 10.3 with Neon dead. A lane won that cleanly leaves room to shove and join that fight. The build also skipped its full winning core (Xenia, Dynamo, Gaia Greaves) outright.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Aurora held an early edge over Khaimera but finished with nine deaths and 45,813 damage taken. The build ran Magnify, Spirit of Amir and Tainted Scepter with no armor item against a comp leaning three-physical, and that gap is the direct line to the damage taken. Aurora was also caught alone by Khaimera at 24.9 minutes, right before the inhibitor fell at 25.9.

5abbc223-5188-4aba-b698-820a7c5a2c00.text: Two solo deaths early, caught by Crunch at 5.2 minutes and by Khaimera at 8.4. Then Terra missed the 16.3 teamfight from an even lane, a fight lost 3-6. Standing alone when the team needed the body showed up more than once.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.text: Kira's lane win over Drongo held all game and the damage output led the team. The build skipped its full winning core (Solaris, Ashbringer, Imperator) for Onixian Quiver and Scattershot instead — worth closing that gap next game.

d9b59cab-b3f3-4044-83d5-2799f376355c.text: Neon: ten deaths and a lane lost to Gideon from start to finish, including a solo catch at 15.4 minutes. Gideon walked away with the game's biggest damage total partly because that lane never got contested back.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.text: Steel shut Sevarog out all game and put up a team-high 12 wards, but sat out the fight at 10.4 near their Fangtooth, lost 1-4. Winning that lane left room to shove and rotate into that fight.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.text: Aurora: nine deaths and 45,813 damage taken against a comp leaning physical, with no armor item bought all game. The damage-taken number follows straight from that build gap.

10.4.call: This fight went 1 kill to 4 near their Fangtooth, and they took that Fangtooth in the same window. Steel was alive and winning his lane against Sevarog at the time and never joined. The fix was shoving that lane and rotating in.

16.3.call: The teamfight at 16.3 at their Inner Tower was lost 3-6, and our own inner tower fell at 17.1 behind it. Terra was alive in a lane reading even, with nothing to hold there, and never joined. An even lane is exactly the one to leave and group from.

29.6.call: This one was a straight fight lost, with no rotation problem to point at: all five were in it, and it still went 0-5 at their Core to end the game.

5abbc223-5188-4aba-b698-820a7c5a2c00.build: Terra's Fire Blossom and Inquisition were the right spine: armor plus a burn aura for the Crunch lane, and magic resist into Gideon's 68k magical damage. The gap was Tainted Guard, the third core piece: it punishes whoever hits her by cutting their healing and leaving a bleed, exactly what Crunch (16,134 health healed) and a diving Khaimera (14,350) feed on. Elafrost and Transference bought more armor and a shield-to-health trick, but neither answers enemy sustain, so both brawlers kept out-healing the extended trades.
5abbc223-5188-4aba-b698-820a7c5a2c00.eternal: Thraex fits Terra's long offlane brawls: her basic attacks mark the target so she hits them harder while taking less back, and Ferocity keeps stacking attack speed the longer the exchange runs, made for grinding down a dueling Crunch. Savage Strikes adds steady on-hit damage to every swing. The trade-off is burst: this loadout pays out over extended contact, so short poke trades and quick disengages get little from it.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Goldilocks324's Vanquisher gave Kira crit, armor piercing, and an execute on low targets, and Scattershot plus Onixian Quiver stacked extra projectiles for spray damage. What never arrived was the winning core around it: Imperator makes every critical strike hit harder, and Ashbringer refunds ability cooldowns on-hit so the ultimate comes back faster. The matchup read said to play this Drongo lane aggressively, and 30,059 hero damage shows the output was there; the crit multiplier and faster ultimates were the missing ceiling in the fights that closed the game out.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Vermis suits Kira's rhythm: every third basic attack on the same target adds damage based on their maximum health, so her sustained fire chews through anyone who stands and fights. Serration adds missing-health damage on the proc to finish what the ramp starts, and Melting Point keeps heavily armored targets from opting out. It trades away safety, since nothing here shields her or helps her escape, so it pays only when she can keep attacking one target uninterrupted.

d9b59cab-b3f3-4044-83d5-2799f376355c.build: Neon's Combustion and Wraith Leggings were two-thirds of the winning core: area burst on ability hits plus flat magic penetration that makes every spell land harder. Azure Core came first instead of finishing with Amulet Of Chaos, whose active resets most of her basic-ability cooldowns and refunds mana, effectively a second full combo in a long fight. Ten deaths into a Gideon lane the pre-game read already called unfavorable meant Azure Core's slow, stack-based payoff never got room to matter; the cooldown-reset item is the one that turns one landed combo into two.
d9b59cab-b3f3-4044-83d5-2799f376355c.eternal: Vesh fits Neon's ability grid: her beams and fields hit repeatedly, and every hit leaves a burn that keeps damaging between volleys. The Tenth Seal boosts her level-10 ultimate and Mind Rot helps the burn wear down frontliners. The trade is protection, none included; with ten deaths this game, the safety this loadout assumes has to come from positioning and peel, because the blessing brings only damage.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Willy Guggenheim built Steel to outlast punishment: Fire Blossom's armor and burn aura, Stonewall's flat physical mitigation, Raiment of Renewal's regeneration, and 56,130 damage taken says the tanking worked. The winning core trades some of that for team output: Xenia shields an ally at the moment they get jumped, and Dynamo makes anyone Steel stuns take extra damage from the whole team. Tainted Charm did bring the healing cut against a lineup with three big self-healers, but as the fourth item; in a game where we won 6 fights and cashed none, the ally-shield and damage-amp tools are what turn won exchanges into kills and towers.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Vesh fits how Steel actually deals damage: his kit is ability-led, and every ability hit leaves a burn that grows as the game runs long. Mind Rot makes that burn scale with the target's current health, so even the enemy frontline feels his crowd-control openers, and The Tenth Seal sharpens the level-10 ultimate window. The cost is durability: nothing in this loadout makes Steel tougher, so it leans on the item build to do the surviving while the blessing does the chip damage.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xeebs took Magnify first, the right opener, and Tainted Scepter was a genuinely good read: it cuts the target's healing, aimed straight at a Khaimera who healed 14,350 health. What the build never added was armor, and the facts flag it: no armor against a three-physical lineup. Elafrost and Gaia Greaves, the skipped core pieces, carry armor and health along with their damage tricks; with nine deaths and 45,813 damage taken, Aurora was freezing targets for the team while melting under basic attacks she had nothing to blunt.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Vesh matches Aurora's ability-first kit: her freezes and area casts each leave a burn behind, so every rotation she lands keeps ticking after she has moved on. Mind Rot points that burn at tanks by adding current-health damage, and The Tenth Seal makes the level-10 ultimate, her big lockdown moment, come up stronger and more often. The trade is that nothing here helps her survive the dive; against a Khaimera who thrives in extended scraps, this loadout wants her to land casts and leave rather than stand and trade.

synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
